name: CJC-1295
lead: CJC-1295 is a synthetic analogue of growth hormone releasing hormone developed in the early 2000s. The long-acting version binds albumin, extending its half-life.
Early human studies showed raised growth hormone and IGF-1, but development stopped and no data show a muscle or cosmetic benefit, so it is rated unproven.

paras: It binds the GHRH receptor on pituitary somatotrophs, increasing growth hormone secretion and IGF-1 levels for days after a single administration in the long-acting form.

It is not an approved medicine, is sold as a research peptide, and is banned in sport. A phase II trial was halted after a death in a participant. Reported effects include flushing, headache, water retention and injection-site reactions. Long-term safety is unknown and the regulatory status of compounded versions has been in flux.
